CISA KEV: CVE-2026-34926 — Trend Micro Apex One (On-Premise) Directory Traversal Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-05-21 1 use case 0 techniques 2 kill-chain phases detected

Trend Micro Apex One (on-premise) contains a directory traversal vulnerability that could allow a pre-authenticated local attacker to modify a key table on the server to inject malicious code to deploy to agents on affected installations. Vendor: Trend Micro, Product: Apex One. Federal patch due: 2026-06-04.

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Nx Console v18.95.0 compromised extension installed (May 2026 supply-chain attack) AIDelivery Medium
Detects installation of the poisoned Nx Console (nrwl.angular-console) v18.95.0 VS Code extension that was published with stolen credentials on 2026-05-18 and pulled by 2.2M+ install base via auto-update. Matches on the known SHA256/SHA1 of the malicious build and the version-pinned extension folder path written by Code.exe / Cursor.exe / node.exe extension hosts. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article-named extension identifier (nrwl.angular-console) and version 18.95.0, plus the four SHA256/SHA1 hashes of the malicious build supplied by the Nx maintainers' advisory. Hashes plus version-pinned path give near-zero FP and cover both fresh installs and offline re-imaging. Cross-checked against GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity's IOC writeup. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR/forensics analyst intentionally retains a copy of the malicious build for triage in a sandbox VM
  • Backup-software snapshot of an already-infected developer endpoint replays the file-write into telemetry
  • Internal threat-intel feed deliberately stages the IOC hashes into a controlled honeypot share
  • Disk-imaging tool restoring an old developer profile that contained the bad version
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msmpeng.exe","sentinelagent.exe","crowdstrike falcon.exe") and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\Quarantine\\","\\Defender\\Scans\\","\\CrowdStrike\\Quarantine\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process is Code.exe / Cursor.exe / Code Helper / node extension host and capture the parent VS Code installation path. Pull DeviceInfo on the host to identify the developer and any cloud/source-code tokens that lived on it. 2) Contain: isolate the device, force-uninstall the extension, and immediately revoke/rotate every credential reachable from that machine — GitHub PATs, npm tokens, AWS keys, SSH keys, Anthropic/Claude tokens, Azure tokens, .env secrets. Search the user's GitHub for any repos created/forked in the exposure window. 3) Hunt: pivot on UC2/UC3/UC4/UC5 across the fleet, search for any orphan-commit fetches to nrwl/nx and outbound DNS-tunneling patterns, and review GitHub audit logs for anomalous repo creations or token usage from the affected accounts.
DeviceFileEvents

VS Code/Cursor extension host fetches dropper from nrwl/nx orphan commit on GitHub AIInstallation Medium
The compromised Nx Console v18.95.0 pulled a 498 KB obfuscated dropper hidden in an orphan (dangling) commit on the legitimate nrwl/nx GitHub repository. This UC hunts VS Code / Cursor / their Node extension-host processes contacting raw.githubusercontent.com or codeload.github.com on nrwl/nx paths — a request shape that the legitimate Nx Console does not make at runtime. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit claim that the 498 KB dropper was hidden in an orphan commit of the legitimate nrwl/nx GitHub repository — a request the unmodified Nx Console extension does not make. Pairs the VS Code / Cursor / extension-host process identity with the unique nrwl/nx GitHub raw/codeload/blob API paths. Cross-checked against GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity which confirm the orphan-commit dropper mechanism. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1102.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer working on the Nx project clones nrwl/nx via VS Code's built-in git integration (path will be /git/refs or /info/refs, not /blobs)
  • VS Code extension recommendation lookup that hits api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx (low-bytes metadata read, not the blob/tree paths)
  • Nx CLI itself fetching update manifests from raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/<release-tag>/ paths
  • Renovate/Dependabot bot acting via the extension host
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("/git/refs","/git/info","/releases/download/")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("renovate","dependabot","semantic-release"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the URL path was a /git/blobs/<sha>, /git/trees/<sha>, or raw URL on a commit hash not present in nrwl/nx's tagged release tree — orphan commits return blobs but aren't reachable from any branch tip. Capture response size; the legitimate use-cases are KB-scale, the dropper was ~498 KB. 2) Contain: isolate the developer endpoint, treat as UC1-confirmed and run the UC1 hashes against DeviceFileEvents. 3) Hunt: extract the commit SHA from RemoteUrl and search the rest of the fleet for the same SHA — the same orphan blob would be fetched by every infected install. Also pivot to DNS for github.com/<unknown-actor-owned>/<repo>/issues which the payload uses as a dead-drop.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","node.exe","code-insiders.exe","codium.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","code-insiders.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees")
   or HttpHostName in~ ("raw.githubusercontent.com","codeload.github.com") and UrlOriginal has "nrwl/nx"
| where SrcUsername != "" and (HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("VSCode","vscode","Cursor","node-fetch","axios","got","undici") or DvcHostname != "")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpResponseBodyBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: VS Code/Cursor Extension Host Fetches nrwl/nx Orphan-Commit Dropper
id: c47e8b95-2a13-4f08-b1d6-7c5e9f3a6e72
description: Detects Code.exe, Cursor.exe or their Node extension host contacting GitHub paths under nrwl/nx (raw, codeload, blob/tree APIs) — the dropper path used by the May 2026 Nx Console v18.95.0 compromise.
references:
    - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/vs-code-extension-github-breach
    - https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
    - attack.t1105
    - attack.t1102.001
    - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_process:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\Code.exe'
            - '\Cursor.exe'
            - '\node.exe'
            - '\Code - Insiders.exe'
            - '\codium.exe'
    selection_destination:
        DestinationHostname|contains:
            - 'raw.githubusercontent.com'

| join({#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 | ContextImageFileName=/(Code|Cursor|node)\.?(exe)?$/i}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], include=[RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where (Web.url IN ("*raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/*","*codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/*","*api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs/*","*api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees/*")) AND Web.src_app IN ("code.exe","cursor.exe","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)") by host Web.dest Web.url Web.src_app Web.user Web.bytes_in | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where bytes_in > 100000 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

macOS Python backdoor persistence via kitty-monitor LaunchAgent and cat.py drop AIInstallation High
After execution, the poisoned Nx Console payload drops a Python backdoor on macOS at ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py and registers a LaunchAgent at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist plus the state file /var/tmp/.gh_update_state. The backdoor uses the GitHub Search API as a dead-drop resolver for follow-on commands. This UC alerts on file creation of any of these named artifacts. Rationale: Anchors on three specific filesystem artifacts disclosed in the GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and corroborated by StepSecurity / The Hacker News: the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent (T1543.001 macOS persistence), the cat.py Python dropper under ~/.local/share/kitty/, and the /var/tmp/.gh_update_state semaphore. None of these names belong to any legitimate kitty terminal install (which doesn't write LaunchAgents under com.user.*). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1102.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher staging the IOC for sandbox analysis on a corporate Mac
  • Defender / CrowdStrike quarantine event re-writing the artifact name into the file path
  • Forensic-image restoration of a previously infected machine in a lab VM
  • User experimenting with the legitimate Kitty terminal — note this uses ~/.config/kitty/, not ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("mdworker","mdworker_shared","backupd","Time Machine") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "com.apple.backupd")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process is python3, node, sh/zsh, or VS Code helper. Identify the GitHub / npm / AWS / Claude credentials accessible to the user on that Mac and the install timestamp of nrwl.angular-console-18.95.0. 2) Contain: kill any python process executing cat.py, unload the LaunchAgent (launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist), delete the four artifacts, isolate the endpoint, and immediately rotate all reachable credentials (GitHub PATs, SSH keys, npm tokens, AWS keys, ~/.claude tokens, .env secrets). 3) Hunt: pivot to UC4 (python __DAEMONIZED=1 process), pull the user's GitHub audit log for repo creations / token usage in the window since installation, and search the rest of the macOS fleet for any of these four paths.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath endswith "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
   or (FolderPath endswith "/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
   or (FolderPath == "/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/kitty-")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetFilePath endswith "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
   or (TargetFilePath endswith "/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
   or (TargetFilePath == "/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
   or (TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/kitty-")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Nx Console Compromise - macOS Python Backdoor Persistence Artifacts
id: d3f9a7c2-6e4b-4a91-8d72-9f1c5b8e2a3d
description: Detects on-disk landing of the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent, cat.py Python backdoor, or /var/tmp/.gh_update_state state file dropped by the compromised Nx Console v18.95.0 VS Code extension.
references:
    - https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w
    - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html

detection:

| (TargetFileName=/\/\.local\/share\/kitty\/cat\.py$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/Library\/LaunchAgents\/com\.user\.kitty-monitor\.plist$/i OR TargetFileName=/^\/var\/tmp\/\.gh_update_state$/i OR TargetFileName=/^\/tmp\/kitty-/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.local/share/kitty/cat.py","*/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist","/var/tmp/.gh_update_state","/tmp/kitty-*") by host Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Python backdoor self-daemonisation via __DAEMONIZED=1 spawned by VS Code helper or node AIInstallation Medium
The Nx Console v18.95.0 macOS backdoor re-execs itself with __DAEMONIZED=1 in its environment to detach from the VS Code extension host parent — a distinctive marker used by cat.py. This UC hunts python processes spawned by code/cursor/node/shell parents that either run cat.py from the kitty directory or carry the __DAEMONIZED=1 token in their command-line / parent command-line. Rationale: The __DAEMONIZED=1 environment-variable self-relaunch is a distinctive marker called out by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity writeup for the cat.py backdoor — legitimate Python tooling does not use this sentinel. Combining it with the kitty/cat.py path and a VS Code helper / node / shell parent yields high fidelity. Cross-checked against GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity IOC list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1564.012 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR analyst replaying a captured payload in a contained VM for triage
  • Detonation sandbox (e.g. ANY.RUN, Joe Sandbox) ingesting the same artifact into corp telemetry
  • Custom DevOps tooling that coincidentally names a script 'cat.py' under a kitty/ subdir (rare — combined with __DAEMONIZED gate this is near-zero)
  • Developer auditing the IOC interactively under their VS Code terminal
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "jupyter" and ProcessCommandLine !has "pytest" and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vscode-python","ms-python.python","debugpy"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full process tree (parent, grandparent), the user, and any open network connections / DNS queries from this PID (pivot to UC2 / DnsRequest). Confirm whether ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py and the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent exist on disk. 2) Contain: kill the python process (and any children), unload the LaunchAgent, delete the artifacts, isolate the endpoint from the network, and rotate every credential reachable from the box including GitHub PATs, SSH keys, npm/AWS/Claude tokens, and .env secrets. 3) Hunt: extract the contacted GitHub Search API query strings from process arguments (used as dead-drop resolver), then sweep the fleet for the same query patterns and for any new repos in the user's GitHub created during/after the install window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","python.exe")

title: Nx Console Compromise - Python cat.py Daemon Spawned by Code Helper or Node

description: Detects the Python backdoor cat.py (or its __DAEMONIZED=1 self-relaunch) launched by a VS Code helper, Cursor helper, node or shell parent. Specific to the May 2026 Nx Console v18.95.0 supply-chain compromise.
references:
    - https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w

    selection_python:

VS Code extension host fan-out reads of developer secrets (.ssh, .aws, .npmrc, ~/.claude/settings.json) AIActions on Objectives Medium
The poisoned Nx Console payload sweeps developer credentials from a fixed list — SSH private keys, AWS credentials, npm tokens, Claude Code config (~/.claude/settings.json — believed to be the first supply-chain payload to target an AI assistant config), gcloud, kube, gnupg, docker, and .env files. This UC alerts when the VS Code / Cursor extension-host Node process touches ≥4 distinct credential-bearing paths within a 10-minute window — a shape no legitimate extension exhibits. Rationale: Anchors on the exact credential-file list disclosed by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity for the cat.py / Nx Console payload, including the novel target ~/.claude/settings.json that the article calls out as one of the first AI-assistant config harvest behaviours seen in the wild. The ≥4-distinct-paths threshold within 10 minutes is a sweep marker that no legitimate VS Code extension exhibits. Cross-checked GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w + StepSecurity + The Hacker News. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Git Credential Manager / gh CLI extension legitimately reading ~/.aws/credentials + ~/.npmrc + ~/.ssh/config during repo clone or push
  • Backup software (Time Machine, restic, borg) snapshotting the entire home directory in one pass
  • SAST/SCA scanners (Snyk, Semgrep, Trufflehog) integrated into VS Code performing a workspace secrets scan
  • Initial workstation provisioning script reading dotfiles for migration
  • Cloud-init or dotfiles-bootstrap tooling running once after a fresh checkout
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git-credential-manager","gh.exe","gh","snyk","semgrep","trufflehog","gitleaks","restic","borg","tmutil","backupd") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vscode-snyk","semgrep-ls","gitlens","github.vscode-pull-request-github"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is the VS Code extension host (node / Code Helper) and not a known credential manager / SAST scanner / backup tool. Pull DeviceFileEvents for the same host within the prior 30 min for the UC1 hashes or UC3 macOS artifacts. 2) Contain: isolate the endpoint and rotate every credential whose path was hit — at minimum GitHub PATs, all SSH keys, AWS access keys, npm tokens, Anthropic/Claude API keys, gcloud refresh tokens, kubeconfig contexts, and every .env reachable. Force a re-clone-from-scratch of any repo where the .env was read. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 (orphan-commit dropper) and UC4 (cat.py daemon) on the same host. Sweep GitHub audit logs for the user's account for repo creations, PAT usage from unfamiliar IPs, and any branch pushes during the install window. Search the npm registry for any packages published by the user's npm account in the same window.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileAccessed","FileRead","FileOpened")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc","settings.json","config.json")
     or FileName =~ ".env" or FileName startswith ".env." or FolderPath has "/.npmrc")
| where not (FolderPath has "/.claude/" and FileName != "settings.json")    // narrow .claude noise — only the settings.json file matters
| summarize PathCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)),
            Paths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 25),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = sweep threshold; one-off .env read is normal dev work, ≥4 distinct cred files in 10 min is harvesting behaviour
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (TargetFilePath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or TargetFileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc")
     or TargetFileName =~ ".env" or TargetFileName startswith ".env."
     or (TargetFilePath has "/.claude/" and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json"))
| summarize PathCount = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = empirical sweep threshold
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) (@process.name:(node OR python OR python3) OR @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *Code\ Helper* OR *cursor-helper* OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe)) (@file.path:(*/.ssh/id_rsa OR */.ssh/id_ed25519 OR */.ssh/id_ecdsa OR */.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.npmrc OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.kube/config OR */.docker/config.json OR */.gnupg/* OR */.claude/settings.json OR */.env OR */.env.*) OR @TargetFilename:(*\\.ssh\\id_rsa OR *\\.aws\\credentials OR *\\.npmrc OR *\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.env))
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/(node|Code Helper|cursor-helper|Cursor|Code|python3?)\.?(exe)?$/i
| (TargetFileName=/\/\.ssh\/(id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|known_hosts|config|authorized_keys)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.npmrc$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.config\/gcloud\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.kube\/config$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.docker\/config\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.gnupg\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.claude\/settings\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.env(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, bucket(span=10m)], function=[count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=PathCount), collect(TargetFileName, multival=true)])
| PathCount >= 4

| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.ssh/id_rsa","*/.ssh/id_ed25519","*/.ssh/id_ecdsa","*/.ssh/known_hosts","*/.ssh/config","*/.aws/credentials","*/.aws/config","*/.npmrc","*/.config/gcloud/*","*/.kube/config","*/.docker/config.json","*/.gnupg/*","*/.claude/settings.json","*/.env","*/.env.*")) AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","python","python3") by host Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 4 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent

| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'

            - '\chrome.exe'

            - '\firefox.exe'

    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser

level: high

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental

    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.

    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Aikido
2026-05-20 8 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

GitHub confirmed a poisoned VS Code extension compromised an employee device, exposing 3,800 internal repos. Why developer workstations are now the top supply chain target. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1190 T1555.003

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Installation. Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS / Network egress to TeamPCP Nx Console C2 domain check.git-service.com · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Burst credential-file harvest by VS Code / node process (Nx Console stealer behaviour) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
DNS / Network egress to TeamPCP Nx Console C2 domain check.git-service.com AICommand & Control High
Hunts any developer endpoint resolving or connecting to check.git-service.com (or sibling subdomains under git-service.com), the credential-exfiltration host used by the TeamPCP Nx Console v18.95.0 supply-chain payload. The domain has no legitimate use — any hit is high-fidelity for the GitHub-breach campaign. Rationale: Domain check.git-service.com is the article's lead IOC; cross-checked via BleepingComputer and StepSecurity write-ups of the same Nx Console v18.95.0 / TeamPCP incident. Any DNS query for this name from a corporate endpoint indicates active credential exfiltration in progress. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/github-confirms-breach-of-3-800-repos-via-malicious-vscode-extension/ • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-internal-repositories-breached.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC analyst triaging the IOC from a jump host (curl/dig/nslookup against the indicator)
  • IOC enrichment tooling (MISP, OpenCTI, TheHive) auto-resolving the domain for context
  • VirusTotal sandbox detonation traffic if VT IDS feed is ingested into the same DNS lake
  • Threat-intel vendor periodic re-resolution of historic IOCs
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","nslookup.exe","dig.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("misp","opencti","thehive","virustotal","--ioc"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm which user, process, and parent process initiated the egress (InitiatingProcessFileName / ContextImageFileName). If Code.exe, node.exe, or npx is in the chain treat as confirmed Nx Console infection on the workstation. 2. Contain: isolate the device via Defender LiveResponse / CS Network Containment, force-rotate every GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS access key, 1Password recovery key, and HashiCorp Vault token bound to that user identity; revoke all GitHub SSH/OAuth grants for the user; invalidate active SSO sessions. 3. Hunt: pivot on AccountName/UserName across the last 30 days for additional egress to git-service.com siblings, recent `git clone` of internal repos from the user's PAT, and any new orphan-commit pushes the stolen token may have made.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where RemoteUrl has "git-service.com" or RemoteIP in ("")
 | extend Source="NetworkEvent"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
(DeviceEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted" or ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
 | where RemoteUrl has "git-service.com" or AdditionalFields has "git-service.com"
 | extend Source="DeviceEvent"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where Name has "git-service.com"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode, Source="DnsEvents"),
(CommonSecurityLog
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where DestinationHostName has "git-service.com" or RequestURL has "git-service.com"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Name=DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
(ImDnsActivity
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where DnsQuery has "git-service.com"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, ResultCode=DnsResponseCodeName, Source="ImDnsActivity")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TeamPCP Nx Console payload SHA256 hash match on developer endpoints AIInstallation Medium
Direct hash-based detection for the four known Nx Console v18.95.0 malicious payload SHA256s — the 2,777-byte injected stub plus the dropped 498KB obfuscated stealer fetched from the nrwl/nx orphan commit. Any write or execution of these binaries on a corporate endpoint is unambiguous compromise. Rationale: Four SHA256s from the article's IOC block; campaign and payload behaviour cross-checked against the official nrwl/nx-console GHSA advisory and StepSecurity analysis. Hash matches on developer endpoints are unambiguous and warrant immediate isolation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.006 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware-analysis sandbox / detonation VM intentionally executing the known sample
  • Endpoint AV/EDR vendor lab machine running the sample for signature tuning
  • SOC reverse-engineering workstation handling the dropped 498KB stealer for IR analysis
  • Aikido / StepSecurity / similar SCA tool quarantining the sample in a controlled location
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ ("malware-sandbox-01","ir-analysis-vm","av-lab-01")
Response runbook
1. Triage: identify the user, parent VS Code process, and timestamp of first hash hit; check whether the device is a sandbox/RE box (allowlist if confirmed). 2. Contain: isolate the host immediately, capture memory if feasible, force rotation of all developer credentials (GitHub PAT, npm token, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.kube/config, ~/.claude/settings.json, 1Password recovery key, HashiCorp Vault tokens) bound to the user, revoke all GitHub OAuth grants and active SSO sessions for that identity. 3. Hunt: pivot the SHA256 fleet-wide for prior sightings, search VS Code extension install telemetry for nrwl.angular-console v18.94.x / v18.95.0, audit GitHub Enterprise audit log for unusual `repo:clone` events from the user's PAT in the prior 30 days.
let TeamPCPHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8","b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74","e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1","43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9"]);
union
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
 | where SHA256 in (TeamPCPHashes)
 | extend EventSource="DeviceFileEvents"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventSource, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
 | where SHA256 in (TeamPCPHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (TeamPCPHashes)
 | extend EventSource="DeviceProcessEvents"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventSource, ActionType="ProcessCreated", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName),
(DeviceImageLoadEvents

 | where SHA256 in (TeamPCPHashes)
 | extend EventSource="DeviceImageLoadEvents"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventSource, ActionType="ImageLoaded", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| order by Timestamp desc
let TeamPCPHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8","b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74","e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1","43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9"]);

VS Code child process fetching payload from nrwl/nx orphan commit (Nx Console v18.95.0 dropper) AIInstallation High
Detects the post-install execution chain unique to the TeamPCP Nx Console compromise: a child process of VS Code (Code.exe / Code - Insiders.exe) invoking npx, node, cmd, or PowerShell with a command line that references either the malicious orphan commit SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2 or raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx — the exact mechanism that pulls down the 498KB obfuscated stealer. Rationale: Pivots on the unique orphan-commit SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2 (confirmed by the nrwl/nx-console GHSA advisory and Nx postmortem) plus the raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx fetch pattern — both are second-source-verified and have no legitimate use. The parent=Code.exe + child=npx/node + URL pattern is unique to the Nx Console v18.95.0 activation flow. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1195.002 T1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Reverse engineer manually re-fetching the orphan-commit blob for analysis from a triage workstation
  • DFIR tooling pulling the IOC from a sandboxed reproduction script
  • Threat intel team mirroring the orphan commit to a private repo for safekeeping (rare)
  • CTF or training exercise reproducing the published attack chain
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("svc-malware-research","svc-dfir") and DeviceName !in~ ("re-vm-01","sandbox-01")
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the user, exact CommandLine, and downstream child processes spawned by the npx/node invocation — record the SHA256 of the dropped file in %TEMP% or ~/.npm/_npx. 2. Contain: isolate the workstation, kill the offending node process tree, rotate every developer credential bound to the user (GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS keys, Claude Code config, 1Password recovery, Vault tokens), revoke GitHub OAuth grants and active SSO sessions. 3. Hunt: enumerate all hosts with VS Code extension nrwl.angular-console v18.94.x–v18.95.0 installed, sweep for the four payload SHA256s, audit GitHub Enterprise audit log for `repo:clone` of internal repositories using the user's PAT in the last 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","code","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code Helper (Renderer)")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","code")
| where FileName in~ ("npx.cmd","npx","node.exe","node","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2","raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx","github.com/nrwl/nx/raw","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where EventID == 4688
 | where ParentProcessName endswith "\\Code.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\Code - Insiders.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\code" or ParentProcessName endswith "Code Helper"
 | where NewProcessName endswith "\\npx.cmd" or NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\cmd.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
 | where CommandLine has_any ("558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2","raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx","github.com/nrwl/nx/raw","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx")
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectAccount, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where ParentProcessName has_any ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","code","Code Helper")
 | where ActingProcessName has_any ("npx","node","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh")
 | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2","raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx","github.com/nrwl/nx/raw","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx")
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: VS Code Child Process Fetching Nx Console v18.95.0 Stealer From nrwl/nx Orphan Commit
id: 9d4e1a82-6c70-4f3b-bd9a-31e2c4f6087d
description: Detects the second-stage payload-fetch chain of the TeamPCP Nx Console supply-chain attack — a process spawned by VS Code (Code.exe / Code - Insiders.exe / Code Helper) running npx, node, cmd, powershell, bash, or sh with a command line that references the orphan commit SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2 or fetches from raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/github-breached-vs-code-extension
  - https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised
  - https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\Code - Insiders.exe'
      - '\Code Helper.exe'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npx.cmd'
      - '\npx'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
  cli:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2'
      - 'raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx'
      - 'github.com/nrwl/nx/raw'
      - 'codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx'
  condition: parent and child and cli
falsepositives:
  - Security researcher pivoting on the orphan-commit SHA from a triage host
level: critical
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\Code.exe OR *\\Code\ -\ Insiders.exe OR *\\code OR *\\Code\ Helper.exe OR *\\Code\ Helper) @Image:(*\\npx.cmd OR *\\npx OR *\\node.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\bash.exe OR *\\sh.exe) @CommandLine:(*558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2* OR *raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx* OR *github.com/nrwl/nx/raw* OR *codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(code|Code|Code - Insiders|Code Helper|Code Helper \(Plugin\)|Code Helper \(Renderer\))(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/(npx(\.cmd)?|node(\.exe)?|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe|bash|sh)$/i
| regex("558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2|raw\\.githubusercontent\\.com/nrwl/nx|github\\.com/nrwl/nx/raw|codeload\\.github\\.com/nrwl/nx", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.parent_process) as pcmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","code","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)") OR match(Processes.parent_process,"(?i)\\\\Code(?:\\s-\\sInsiders)?\\.exe")) (Processes.process_name IN ("npx.cmd","npx","node.exe","node","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh") AND (Processes.process="*558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2*" OR Processes.process="*raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx*" OR Processes.process="*github.com/nrwl/nx/raw*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.parent_process) as pcmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","code","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)") OR match(Processes.parent_process,"(?i)\\\\Code(?:\\s-\\sInsiders)?\\.exe")) (Processes.process_name IN ("npx.cmd","npx","node.exe","node","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh") AND (Processes.process="*558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2*" OR Processes.process="*raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx*" OR Processes.process="*github.com/nrwl/nx/raw*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Burst credential-file harvest by VS Code / node process (Nx Console stealer behaviour) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the credential-collection burst pattern executed by the Nx Console v18.95.0 stealer: a single Code.exe or node.exe process touching five or more distinct credential/secret files (.env, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.kube/config, ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.config/1Password) within a 5-minute window. The behaviour mirrors the published payload's documented target list across GitHub / npm / AWS / 1Password / HashiCorp Vault / Kubernetes / Anthropic Claude Code. Rationale: Implements the credential-harvest signature documented in the article (the payload 'read .env files') and corroborated by StepSecurity / nrwl postmortem (targets npm, GitHub, AWS, 1Password, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, Anthropic Claude Code). The 5-distinct-paths-in-5-minutes threshold catches the burst behaviour while suppressing normal developer dotenv usage which typically touches 1-2 files. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1083 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running a legit credential-rotation or `aws configure` flow that touches multiple cred files in quick succession
  • Backup/sync tool (Dropbox, OneDrive, Time Machine) re-indexing a dotfile-heavy home directory under a node.exe context
  • CI runner agent (GitHub Actions self-hosted, GitLab runner) seeding multiple credentials at job start
  • IaC tooling (Terraform, Pulumi) using node-based providers that read AWS + kube + npm configs together
  • Repo-search / code-intel extensions (e.g. ripgrep wrappers, source-graph) scanning workspaces that legitimately contain .env files
Suppression filter
| where Cmd !contains "aws configure" and Cmd !contains "gh auth" and Cmd !contains "terraform" and InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$" and not (DeviceName startswith "ci-runner-" or DeviceName startswith "gha-runner-")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine + parent process. If parent=Code.exe and the node process has no obvious workspace package.json invocation context, treat as suspicious. Capture the dropped output files (often staged in %TEMP%, ~/.npm/_npx, or /tmp) and hash them. 2. Contain: isolate the host, terminate the node process tree, rotate every credential class seen in the file list (GitHub PAT, npm, AWS, Claude Code, 1Password recovery, Vault). 3. Hunt: pivot AccountName across the fleet for the same 5-in-5min pattern, search DNS for git-service.com beacons from the same host in the same window, and audit GitHub Enterprise / npm / AWS CloudTrail for any privileged action using the rotated credentials in the prior 7 days.
let CredPathFragments = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @"\.npmrc", @"/.npmrc", @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config", @"\.claude\settings.json", @"/.claude/settings.json", @"\.config\1Password", @"/.config/1Password", @"\.docker\config.json", @"vault-token", @".gitconfig"]);
let CredFileNames = dynamic([".env",".envrc","credentials",".npmrc",".pypirc","settings.json","config","vault-token"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper.exe")
| where (FolderPath has_any (CredPathFragments)) or (FileName in~ (CredFileNames) and FolderPath !contains "node_modules")
| summarize DistinctPaths = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)), SamplePaths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
  by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 5
| order by FirstSeen desc
let CredPathFragments = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @".npmrc", @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config", @"\.claude\settings.json", @"/.claude/settings.json", @"\.config\1Password", @"/.config/1Password", @"\.docker\config.json", @"vault-token"]);
let CredFileNames = dynamic([".env",".envrc","credentials",".npmrc",".pypirc","settings.json","vault-token"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper")
| where (TargetFilePath has_any (CredPathFragments)) or (TargetFileName in~ (CredFileNames) and TargetFilePath !contains "node_modules")
| summarize DistinctPaths = dcount(TargetFilePath), SamplePaths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
  by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 5
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\Code\ -\ Insiders.exe OR *\\Code\ Helper.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\\.env OR *\\.envrc OR *\\.aws\\credentials OR *\\.npmrc OR *\\.kube\\config OR *\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.config\\1Password* OR *\\.docker\\config.json OR *vault-token*) -@TargetFilename:*\\node_modules\\*
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| ContextImageFileName=/(node(\.exe)?|Code(\.exe)?|Code - Insiders\.exe|Code Helper(\.exe)?)$/i
| regex("\\\\\\.env$|\\\\\\.envrc$|\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|/\\.aws/credentials|\\\\\\.npmrc|/\\.npmrc|\\\\\\.kube\\\\config|/\\.kube/config|\\\\\\.claude\\\\settings\\.json|/\\.claude/settings\\.json|\\\\\\.config\\\\1Password|/\\.config/1Password|\\\\\\.docker\\\\config\\.json|vault-token", field=TargetFileName)
| TargetFileName!=/node_modules/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName], function=count(as=distinct_hits))
| distinct_hits>=5
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as touched_files dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.env*" OR Filesystem.file_name=".env" OR Filesystem.file_name=".envrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_name=".npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.claude\\settings.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.claude/settings.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\1Password*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/1Password*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.docker\\config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_name="vault-token") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.process_name _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 5
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as touched_files dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.env*" OR Filesystem.file_name=".env" OR Filesystem.file_name=".envrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_name=".npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.claude\\settings.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.claude/settings.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\1Password*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/1Password*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.docker\\config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_name="vault-token") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.process_name _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 5
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] WormFrp / Webworm Amazon S3 staging bucket access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
EchoCreep Discord API beacon from non-browser process (Webworm 2025) AICommand & Control High
Hunts the EchoCreep backdoor's Discord-based C2 channel: a script interpreter or non-browser process beaconing to discord.com / discordapp.com API endpoints to upload files, fetch jobs, and run cmd.exe shell commands. ESET decrypted 400+ Discord messages and four guild/channel pairs tied to this campaign. Rationale: Article anchors EchoCreep to Discord API calls for upload/download/shell/sleep (Table 1) and explicitly states the backdoor's network traffic 'passes through Discord APIs using crafted HTTP requests'. Excluding the genuine Discord client + browsers leaves only the C2 path. Cross-checked Mandiant's Discord-C2 pattern guidance to confirm exclusion list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://www.symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod or curl.exe against Discord webhooks for legitimate notifications
  • Game launchers (non-Discord) embedding Discord rich-presence calls via custom binaries
  • Custom helpdesk bots calling Discord API from a scheduled task using powershell.exe
  • Security tools that fetch indicator feeds from Discord-hosted gists
  • First-party Discord beta builds with non-standard EXE names
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("webhooks/","@everyone","slash-command") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("devops","build-bot"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and parent chain; if it's a script interpreter spawned by Office, browser, or unknown parent, escalate. Validate the user's intent (do they own a Discord bot script?). 2) Contain — isolate the host via Defender LiveResponse, kill the InitiatingProcessId, and block the destination Discord channel ID at the proxy if extractable from packet capture. 3) Hunt — search 30 days for the same parent-process hash across the estate, pivot on InitiatingProcessFolderPath for staged binaries, and query DeviceFileEvents for any GitHub-staged droppers (SoftEther, iox, frp) on the same host.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Discord.exe","DiscordPTB.exe","DiscordCanary.exe","Spotify.exe","slack.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WebexTeams.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, NewProcessId;
let DiscordTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
       or Url has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/","discord.com/api","discordapp.com/api")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
DiscordTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstNet desc
