Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Microsoft's durabletask package on PyPi Compromised. Mini Shai Hulud attacks aga
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] durabletask PyPI dropper launches second-stage zipapp (python3 /tmp/managed.pyz) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 / payload-host resolution to check.git-service.com (durabletask worm) · [LLM] FIRESCALE GitHub dead-drop fallback C2 lookup (api.github.com commit search) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Kubernetes propagation via kubectl staged in /tmp (kubectl exec / get secrets) · [LLM] Single process fan-out reading cloud, Vault, SSH and AI-tool credential files · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
durabletask PyPI dropper launches second-stage zipapp (python3 /tmp/managed.pyz) AIInstallation High
Hunts the import-time dropper injected into durabletask 1.4.1-1.4.3, which urlretrieves rope.pyz to /tmp/managed.pyz and executes it via a detached python3 process. The fixed /tmp/managed.pyz path executed by a Python parent is the article-specific signature of the second-stage launch. Rationale: Anchored on the exact hardcoded drop path /tmp/managed.pyz that the urllib.request.urlretrieve dropper writes and python3 executes; this path executed by a Python interpreter is unique to this campaign. Cross-checked Endor Labs and Wiz write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/trojanized-microsoft-sdk-durabletask-1-4-1-through-1-4-3-deliver-credential-stealing-malware • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://github.com/microsoft/durabletask-python/issues/137
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher detonating the sample in a managed sandbox
  • Internal malware-analysis lab re-running the zipapp
  • A developer manually copying an unrelated .pyz to /tmp/managed.pyz (extremely rare given exact name)
  • IR responders replaying the payload during forensics
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent chain — a python3 process whose grandparent installed/imported durabletask; pull installed pip version (durabletask 1.4.1/1.4.2/1.4.3 = confirmed malicious). 2) Contain: kill the detached python3 PID and any /tmp/managed.pyz, isolate the host, rotate every cloud/SSH/Vault credential reachable from it, and pin durabletask back to 1.4.0. 3) Hunt: search the whole estate for /tmp/managed.pyz, /tmp/kubectl, and outbound git-service.com traffic; review CI/CD runners which most commonly import this SDK.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz" or FolderPath =~ "/tmp/managed.pyz"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz" or TargetProcessName endswith "managed.pyz"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

C2 / payload-host resolution to check.git-service.com (durabletask worm) AICommand & Control High
Hunts DNS resolution and network egress to the attacker-controlled lookalike domain check.git-service.com (and git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com) used to fetch rope.pyz and check in at /v1/models. A three-day-old NameSilo privacy-guarded domain masquerading as a git service is a clean campaign IOC. Rationale: check.git-service.com is the byte-for-byte identical payload URL/C2 across all three trojanized versions; a brand-new privacy-guarded lookalike resolving from dev/CI hosts is near-zero-FP. Domain confirmed by SafeDep and Wiz. Datadog left empty: Linux DNS has no standard Datadog source schema in this tenant. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sinkhole / takedown infrastructure now resolving the seized domain
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling actively probing the IOC
  • Sandbox detonation generating the lookup
  • Security scanner validating the IOC list
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the process behind the resolution (expect python3); confirm whether rope.pyz (/rope.pyz) was fetched and /v1/models was contacted. 2) Contain: block git-service.com and m-kosche.com at DNS/proxy/egress firewall, isolate resolving hosts, and rotate exposed secrets. 3) Hunt: pivot on every host that resolved the domain, then check those hosts for /tmp/managed.pyz execution and outbound api.github.com FIRESCALE searches (fallback channel).

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity

| where DnsQuery has "git-service.com" or DnsQuery has "m-kosche.com"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, DvcHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

FIRESCALE GitHub dead-drop fallback C2 lookup (api.github.com commit search) AICommand & Control High
Hunts the worm's censorship-resistant fallback: a GitHub commit-search request for the string FIRESCALE used to retrieve an RSA-signed replacement C2 address. The literal token FIRESCALE in a request URL to GitHub's commit search API is a unique, essentially zero-FP campaign signature requiring URL-level proxy/web telemetry. Rationale: FIRESCALE is the unique cleartext marker the payload searches GitHub commit history for (api.github.com/search/commits?q=FIRESCALE), making any URL containing it on api.github.com a definitive IOC. Falcon/Datadog left empty: HTTPS query strings aren't shipped in FDR DNS/NetworkConnect records — needs proxy URL logging. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/trojanized-microsoft-sdk-durabletask-1-4-1-through-1-4-3-deliver-credential-stealing-malware
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer legitimately searching GitHub for a project/string literally named FIRESCALE
  • Threat-intel analyst manually querying the same commit-search API to track the actor
  • Sandbox detonation triggering the fallback when the primary C2 is down
  • Security tooling crawling the IOC
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the requesting process is python3 (not a browser/git user) and that the primary C2 (git-service.com) was already unreachable — fallback only fires then. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block api.github.com egress for non-developer service accounts, and rotate reachable secrets. 3) Hunt: the fallback proves active worm logic — sweep for /tmp/managed.pyz, AWS SSM SendCommand fan-out, and kubectl exec propagation across the estate.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "FIRESCALE"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "FIRESCALE" and (HttpHostName has "api.github.com" or Url has "github.com")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DvcHostname, HttpHostName, Url, UserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Kubernetes propagation via kubectl staged in /tmp (kubectl exec / get secrets) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the worm's Kubernetes spread: it downloads kubectl from the official CDN to /tmp/kubectl when not already installed, then uses kubectl exec to propagate and dumps every secret in every namespace. Execution of a kubectl binary from /tmp is highly anomalous and article-specific. Rationale: Legitimate kubectl lives in /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin; the worm explicitly fetches it to /tmp/kubectl, so any process at /tmp/kubectl is the campaign-specific propagation step. Kubernetes targeting corroborated by Upwind. Parent will typically be the python3 payload. Cross-checked against: • https://www.upwind.io/feed/newly-discovered-durabletask-malware-targeted-kubernetes-cloud-secrets-and-ci-cd-infrastructure • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1609 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • An engineer manually curling kubectl to /tmp for a one-off test on a host without it installed
  • CI job that downloads kubectl to a temp dir (usually a build workdir, not literally /tmp/kubectl)
  • Ephemeral troubleshooting container fetching kubectl
  • Air-gapped node bootstrap script staging kubectl
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "python" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "managed.pyz" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("exec","get secret","get secrets")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the parent of /tmp/kubectl (expect python3 from /tmp/managed.pyz) and review its args for 'exec' or 'get secret' across namespaces/contexts. 2) Contain: isolate the node, revoke the in-cluster service-account token and any ~/.kube/config credentials it touched, and audit RBAC for the identity used. 3) Hunt: enumerate kubectl exec events across the cluster (AKSAudit pods/exec) and rotate every Kubernetes secret that was readable from the compromised context.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath == "/tmp/kubectl" or ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/kubectl"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/tmp/kubectl" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/kubectl"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: durabletask Worm kubectl Staged in /tmp
id: 9b4e2d6a-7c1f-4a8b-3d5e-6f2a1c4b8d55
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of a kubectl binary downloaded to /tmp by the durabletask worm for Kubernetes propagation and secret dumping.
references:
  - https://www.upwind.io/feed/newly-discovered-durabletask-malware-targeted-kubernetes-cloud-secrets-and-ci-cd-infrastructure
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/26
tags:
  - attack.t1609
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image: '/tmp/kubectl'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: '/tmp/kubectl'
  condition: selection_img or selection_cmd
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.executable.path:/tmp/kubectl OR @process.command_line:*/tmp/kubectl*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/tmp\/kubectl$/i
| table([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName])
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/tmp/kubectl*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/tmp/kubectl*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| sort - lastTime
Single process fan-out reading cloud, Vault, SSH and AI-tool credential files AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the infostealer's collection stage: one process (the python3 payload) accessing a large, diverse set of hardcoded secret paths — AWS/Azure/GCP creds, ~/.kube/config, ~/.vault-token, ~/.ssh, ~/.pypirc/.npmrc, and notably AI-tooling configs like ~/.cursor/mcp.json and ~/.codeium/mcp.json. The breadth across unrelated secret stores from one PID is the signal. Rationale: The article lists 90+ hardcoded paths; the high-fidelity discriminator is one process touching mutually-unrelated secret stores (cloud + Vault + SSH + npm/pypi + AI-tool MCP configs) — legitimate tools read one family, not all. The AI-tooling configs (~/.cursor/mcp.json, ~/.codeium/mcp.json) are unusual collection targets and rarely read en masse. Note: Linux file-read telemetry coverage varies (auditd watches / FileOpenInfo) — Datadog/Sigma omitted as this is a count/fan-out, not a single-event shape. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud • https://snyk.io/blog/durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A backup or dotfile-sync agent (e.g. restic, rclone) reading the home directory wholesale
  • An endpoint DLP/secret scanner (gitleaks, trufflehog) walking the filesystem
  • A developer's IDE indexing the home folder including .ssh and .aws
  • Configuration-management agent (Ansible/Chef) templating multiple credential files
  • Legitimate cloud SDK credential-chain resolution touching several provider files
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("gitleaks", "trufflehog", "rclone", "restic", "ansible") and not (InitiatingProcessFileName has "code" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "server")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the accessing process — a python3 process (especially parented by /tmp/managed.pyz) reading cloud + Vault + AI-tool configs together is malicious; benign scanners have recognisable binary names. 2) Contain: isolate the host and treat ALL credentials in the touched files as compromised — rotate AWS/Azure/GCP keys, Vault tokens, SSH keys, npm/PyPI tokens, and any MCP-stored API keys. 3) Hunt: correlate with outbound git-service.com exfil and look for the same fan-out pattern on other hosts that imported durabletask.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has_any (".aws/credentials", ".kube/config", ".vault-token", ".azure/accessTokens.json", ".npmrc", ".pypirc", ".ssh/", ".cursor/mcp.json", ".codeium/mcp.json", "claude_desktop_config.json")
| summarize DistinctSecrets = dcount(FolderPath), Files = make_set(FolderPath, 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where DistinctSecrets >= 5
| order by DistinctSecrets desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (".aws/credentials", ".kube/config", ".vault-token", ".azure/accessTokens.json", ".npmrc", ".pypirc", ".ssh/", ".cursor/mcp.json", ".codeium/mcp.json", "claude_desktop_config.json")
| summarize DistinctSecrets = dcount(TargetFilePath), Files = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where DistinctSecrets >= 5
| order by DistinctSecrets desc
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo TargetFileName=/(\.aws\/credentials|\.kube\/config|\.vault-token|\.azure\/accessTokens\.json|\.npmrc|\.pypirc|\.ssh\/|\.cursor\/mcp\.json|\.codeium\/mcp\.json|claude_desktop_config\.json)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctSecrets))
| DistinctSecrets >= 5
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` dc(Filesystem.file_path) as DistinctSecrets values(Filesystem.file_path) as files min(_time) as firstTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.vault-token" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/accessTokens.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.pypirc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cursor/mcp.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.codeium/mcp.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*claude_desktop_config.json") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_id
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where DistinctSecrets >= 5
| sort - DistinctSecrets
| tstats summariesonly=false dc(Filesystem.file_path) as DistinctSecrets values(Filesystem.file_path) as files min(_time) as firstTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.vault-token" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/accessTokens.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.pypirc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cursor/mcp.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.codeium/mcp.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*claude_desktop_config.json") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_id
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where DistinctSecrets >= 5
| sort - DistinctSecrets
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

2026-05-19 14 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Mini Shai-Hulud strikes again: npm worm compromises hundreds of @antv packages
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm payload by SHA256 · [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud persistence hooks written into .vscode/ and .claude/ configs · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud C2 exfil to t.m-kosche.com disguised as OpenTelemetry collector · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping via /proc · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Mini Shai-Hulud C2 exfil to t.m-kosche.com disguised as OpenTelemetry collector AICommand & Control High
Hunts outbound connections/DNS to the campaign's fallback C2 t.m-kosche.com, which receives RSA-encrypted stolen credentials over OpenTelemetry-style paths (/api/public/otel/v1/traces) on 443. The domain is unique to this campaign and confirmed by multiple vendors, making any contact high-fidelity. Rationale: Anchored on the campaign-unique C2 domain t.m-kosche.com confirmed by StepSecurity, Microsoft, Snyk and JFrog write-ups; the OTel path /api/public/otel/v1/traces detail was added from cross-referenced sources. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-antv-ecosystem • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researchers/sandboxes deliberately detonating the sample and beaconing to the domain
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling resolving the IOC domain for reputation lookups
  • DNS sinkhole already redirecting m-kosche.com (resolution still logged)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host/CI runner and the InitiatingProcess (node/npm/python) that resolved m-kosche.com; pull the surrounding process tree and any npm install in scope. 2) Contain: block t.m-kosche.com at egress/DNS, isolate the host, and freeze the associated CI pipeline; treat every secret reachable from that environment as compromised and begin rotation. 3) Hunt: pivot org-wide on the @antv/timeago/echarts-for-react package versions, search GitHub for repos created with the reversed 'niagA oG eW ereH' description, and check for .claude/.vscode persistence writes.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "m-kosche.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has "m-kosche.com"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm payload by SHA256 AIInstallation Medium
Detects the worm's obfuscated payload file landing or executing on a host by its confirmed SHA256 hashes. High-fidelity exact-match IOC for the AntV-wave payload. Rationale: Uses the two pre-extracted SHA256 payload hashes as exact-match file/process IOCs — zero ambiguity, only ships because the campaign is documented by multiple vendors. Cross-checked against: • https://www.snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst copying the sample onto an analysis VM
  • EDR quarantine/restore operations re-touching the file
  • Threat-intel YARA scanning repos that contain a stored copy of the sample
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the file path and the process that wrote/executed it; determine if this is a dev workstation or a CI runner. 2) Contain: isolate host, kill the node/python chain, and rotate every credential reachable from the environment (AWS/GCP/Azure/K8s/Vault/npm tokens). 3) Hunt: sweep for the C2 domain m-kosche.com, the compromised @antv package versions in lockfiles, and .vscode/.claude persistence artifacts across the fleet.

GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping via /proc AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the worm's embedded Python helper that scans /proc for the Runner.Worker process and reads its memory to recover masked CI/CD secrets in plaintext. Targets Linux CI runners where a node/npm-spawned interpreter references Runner.Worker or /proc/<pid>/mem. Rationale: Anchored on the campaign-specific Runner.Worker /proc memory-scraping technique (the novel CI secret-recovery method) corroborated by Microsoft and the Securonix beta analytic; scoped to npm/node-spawned interpreters to cut noise. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://connect.securonix.com/threat-research-intelligence-62/beta-detection-mini-shai-hulud-runner-worker-memory-secret-extraction-analytic-308
ATT&CKT1003.007 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate CI debugging tooling (gdb, strace, custom memory profilers) inspecting Runner.Worker
  • Self-hosted runner health/diagnostic scripts that read /proc
  • Security agents legitimately scanning /proc memory
  • Performance profilers using process_vm_readv
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("gdb","strace","perf ","datadog-agent","falcon-sensor"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent is a node/npm install step rather than an approved diagnostic; capture the full command line and the package being installed. 2) Contain: cancel the workflow run, revoke the runner's token, and immediately rotate ALL repository/org Actions secrets (they must be assumed exfiltrated regardless of masking). 3) Hunt: check egress to m-kosche.com from the runner, review recent npm publishes from the same maintainer token, and audit GitHub for worm-created repos.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/self/mem","process_vm_readv") or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/[0-9]+/mem"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx","sh","bash","python","python3")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has "Runner.Worker" or SyslogMessage has_any ("/proc/self/mem","process_vm_readv")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("node","npm","python")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud persistence hooks written into .vscode/ and .claude/ configs AIInstallation Medium
Detects node/npm/npx processes writing into .vscode/ or .claude/ configuration directories, where the worm plants auto-execution hooks that survive across sessions and cloned repos. Combination of a JS toolchain process touching these trusted IDE/agent config dirs is the article-specific signal. Rationale: Anchored on the worm's documented persistence in .claude/ and .vscode/ trusted config dirs (Akamai/Microsoft); scopes to the JS toolchain (node/npm/npx) as the writing process to separate from normal IDE activity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/mini-shai-hulud-worm-returns-goes-public • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/
ATT&CKT1554 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developers legitimately running npm scripts that scaffold .vscode/settings.json or tasks.json
  • VS Code extension installers writing into .vscode
  • Project generators (create-react-app, nx, vite) emitting .vscode workspace configs
  • Claude Code itself writing into .claude during normal use
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("create-react-app","vite","nx ","yo ","degit") )
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the written .vscode/tasks.json or .claude config and inspect for auto-run commands, embedded scripts, or network callouts; correlate with a recent npm install of an @antv/timeago package. 2) Contain: remove the malicious config entries, isolate the host, and rotate credentials accessible from the dev environment. 3) Hunt: check the host and any repos cloned from it for the same persistence files, look for egress to m-kosche.com, and search version control for committed .vscode/.claude hooks pushed by stolen tokens.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath contains ".vscode" or FolderPath contains ".claude"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm","npx.cmd","npx")
| where FileName endswith ".json" or FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".sh"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has ".vscode" or TargetFilePath has ".claude"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","npx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:

detection:

            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:

falsepositives:

    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

actions-cool/issues-helper GitHub Action Compromised: All Tags Point to Imposter Commit That Exfiltrates CI/CD Credentials

StepSecurity
2026-05-19 6 use cases 0 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The popular GitHub Action actions-cool/issues-helper has been compromised. Every existing tag in the repository has been moved to point to a single imposter commit that does not appear in the action's normal commit history. That commit contains malicious code that exfiltrates credentials from CI/CD pipelines that run the action.

Domainst.m-kosche.com

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GitHub workflow references actions-cool/issues-helper or maintain-one-comment by tag
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — actions-cool/issues-helper GitHub Action Compromised: All Tags Point to Imposter
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] bun runtime executed on CI runner spawning python3 with sudo escalation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound C2 to t.m-kosche.com from CI/CD runner or any endpoint · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] python3 reading /proc/<PID>/mem to scrape Runner.Worker secrets
Outbound C2 to t.m-kosche.com from CI/CD runner or any endpoint AICommand & Control High
Hunts the exfiltration callback used by the compromised actions-cool/issues-helper and actions-cool/maintain-one-comment GitHub Actions. Any DNS resolution or HTTPS connection to t.m-kosche.com from a runner, developer workstation, or build agent indicates secrets-in-flight exfiltration. Rationale: Pure-IOC detection on t.m-kosche.com — the attacker-controlled exfil domain named explicitly in the StepSecurity advisory and corroborated by The Hacker News, GBHackers, and SC Media. The domain is on the Harden-Runner global block list. Cross-checked with the StepSecurity X post and the Mini Shai-Hulud cluster note from coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html • https://gbhackers.com/compromised-github-action/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/compromised-github-action-exfiltrates-workflow-credentials/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate research traffic from a sandbox / detonation chamber that intentionally resolves IOC domains
  • Threat-intel platforms (MISP, ThreatConnect) doing enrichment lookups against the domain
  • Security analyst manually browsing the StepSecurity advisory and clicking embedded IOC links
  • Harden-Runner audit-mode telemetry that intentionally allows the call so it can be logged before blocking
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","misp","threatintel") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: identify the source host/runner from DeviceName / ClientIP / aid. Pull the full process tree on the source (parent process of the resolver / connector — look for bun, node, python3). 2. Contain: if a self-hosted runner, pull the runner offline; if a developer workstation, isolate the endpoint. Rotate ANY secrets exposed to recent workflow runs on the affected repository, especially GITHUB_TOKEN, repo secrets, and OIDC-issued cloud credentials. 3. Hunt: enumerate every workflow run in the org that referenced actions-cool/issues-helper or actions-cool/maintain-one-comment in the last 30 days; pin all third-party actions to immutable commit SHAs going forward; search audit logs for unauthorized PRs/commits made with the leaked GITHUB_TOKEN.

  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","ConnectionSuccess")
  | where RemoteUrl has exfil_domain or AdditionalFields has exfil_domain
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, AdditionalFields)
| order by Timestamp desc
let exfil_domain = "m-kosche.com";
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name has exfil_domain | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ServerIPAddress),
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationHostName has exfil_domain or RequestURL has exfil_domain or DestinationDnsDomain has exfil_domain | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, SourceUserName),
(ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has exfil_domain | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, DnsQueryType, DnsResponseName),
(ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Url has exfil_domain or HttpHostName has exfil_domain | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: actions-cool issues-helper Exfil Domain Callback (t.m-kosche.com)
id: 7d3a4e5b-9c1f-4f72-b6a0-6b2f4e9d1c84
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS resolution or HTTPS connection to t.m-kosche.com, the exfiltration domain used by the compromised actions-cool/issues-helper and actions-cool/maintain-one-comment GitHub Actions to receive secrets harvested from Runner.Worker memory.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1567
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - 'm-kosche.com'
      - '.m-kosche.com'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - None expected. The domain is attacker-controlled and listed on the Harden-Runner global block list.
level: high
(@dns.question.name:(*m-kosche.com OR *.m-kosche.com) OR @network.destination.name:(*m-kosche.com OR *.m-kosche.com) OR @http.url:(*m-kosche.com* OR *M-KOSCHE.COM*) OR @url.domain:(m-kosche.com OR *.m-kosche.com))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)m-kosche\.com$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/(bun|node|python3|curl|wget)/i) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count()) | sort(field=_count, order=desc)
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src values(DNS.query) as query from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*m-kosche.com" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*m-kosche.com*" OR Web.dest="*m-kosche.com*" by Web.src Web.dest Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | append [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest="*m-kosche.com*" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src values(DNS.query) as query from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*m-kosche.com" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*m-kosche.com*" OR Web.dest="*m-kosche.com*" by Web.src Web.dest Web.url | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest="*m-kosche.com*" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`]
python3 reading /proc/<PID>/mem to scrape Runner.Worker secrets AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the exact credential-harvesting primitive used by the compromised actions-cool actions: a python3 process opening another process's /proc/<PID>/mem to scrape decrypted GitHub Actions secrets from Runner.Worker memory. The behaviour is rare on legitimate CI/CD runners and developer Linux endpoints. Rationale: Anchors on the exact behaviour the article and StepSecurity Harden-Runner traces describe: python3 reading /proc/<PID>/mem against the Runner.Worker process (PID 2119 in their controlled test) and grep-filtering for `isSecret`:true tokens. Cross-process /proc/<PID>/mem reads by python on Linux are a high-fidelity credential-access signal — this is essentially T1003.007 in script form. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/007/
ATT&CKT1003.007 T1552.001 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR teams running memory acquisition tools (avml, lime, volatility) on Linux endpoints
  • Developers debugging their own application by reading /proc/self/mem
  • Container security scanners that introspect process memory of running workloads
  • Performance-profiling agents (py-spy, pyflame) that attach to other Python processes
  • Legitimate use of bun/node memory analysis tooling during CI for performance regression tests
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("avml","lime","volatility","py-spy","strace","gdb") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("avml","lime","strace","gdb")
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the python3 invocation's parent process tree. If parent is `bun` or the GitHub Actions runner (`Runner.Listener` / `Runner.Worker`), it's the attack chain — almost no legitimate workflow shells from bun into python3 reading runner memory. Pull the full command line and resolve the PID being read. 2. Contain: kill the python3 process, take the runner offline, snapshot disk for IR. Rotate every secret that ever touched that runner's workflows in the last 30d (GITHUB_TOKEN, OIDC-issued cloud creds, registry credentials, repo / org / environment secrets). 3. Hunt: search org-wide for the same parent→child chain (bun → python3 → /proc/*/mem) and for any callbacks to t.m-kosche.com or related Mini Shai-Hulud infrastructure; audit recent commits and PRs created via affected GITHUB_TOKENs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName matches regex @"^python3?(\.\d+)?$" or InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"^python3?(\.\d+)?$"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/mem"
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("isSecret","Runner.Worker")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/mem"
| extend ProcMemTarget = extract(@"/proc/(\d+)/mem", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcMemTarget, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
  | where Facility in ("authpriv","auth","daemon","user")
  | where SyslogMessage matches regex @"(?i)python3?[^\s]*\s+[^\n]*/proc/\d+/mem"
     or SyslogMessage has_any ("isSecret","Runner.Worker")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
  | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)python3?(\.\d+)?$"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/mem"
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("isSecret","Runner.Worker")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Python Process Reading /proc/<PID>/mem (CI Runner Memory Scrape)
id: 2b8f1a64-3d97-4d8c-9c0e-1b2af3b6e711
status: experimental
description: Detects a python interpreter executed with a /proc/<PID>/mem path in its command line, the credential-dump primitive used by the compromised actions-cool/issues-helper and actions-cool/maintain-one-comment GitHub Actions to scrape Runner.Worker memory and exfiltrate decrypted secrets tagged "isSecret":true.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1003.007
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1059.006
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|re: '/proc/\d+/mem'
  selection_str:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'isSecret'
      - 'Runner.Worker'
  condition: selection_proc and (selection_cmd or selection_str)
falsepositives:
  - Forensic / memory-acquisition tooling (volatility, lime, avml) operated by IR teams
  - Debugging by developers reading their own process memory for diagnostics
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) (@process.executable.path:(*/python3 OR */python OR */python3.* OR */PYTHON3) OR @process.name:(python3 OR python OR PYTHON3)) (@process.command_line:*\/proc\/* AND @process.command_line:*\/mem*) OR @process.command_line:*isSecret* OR @process.command_line:*Runner.Worker*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/python3?(\.\d+)?$/i | regex("/proc/\d+/mem|isSecret|Runner\.Worker", field=CommandLine) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count()) | sort(field=_count, order=desc)

bun runtime executed on CI runner spawning python3 with sudo escalation AIInstallation High
Hunts the install-stage of the actions-cool/issues-helper compromise: the imposter commit's index.js downloads the bun JavaScript runtime onto the runner, which then spawns python3 via sudo to read Runner.Worker memory. The bun→python3→sudo chain is the article's signature behaviour. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim chain: `bun` runtime (which the imposter commit explicitly downloads to the runner) spawning python3, sudo, and `gh auth token`. This combination is essentially unique to the attack — bun is a JS runtime, not a Python wrapper, and bun→sudo is anomalous in any normal CI workflow. Cross-checked against StepSecurity Harden-Runner test run capture (linked in advisory) and confirmed by Hacker News + GBHackers coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html • https://gbhackers.com/compromised-github-action/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1548.003 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A bun-based project's postinstall script that legitimately shells out to a Python build helper (rare in practice)
  • Developer workstations where bun is used as a general-purpose script runner and the user manually invokes sudo / gh from a bun REPL
  • CI workflows that intentionally use bun to orchestrate multi-language builds with Python steps
  • Bun's own self-update mechanism invoking sudo to install to /usr/local
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "bun" and FileName == "sudo" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("apt-get","dnf","yum","npm install -g","bun upgrade"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the GitHub Actions workflow run identifier from the runner's environment and confirm whether the workflow referenced actions-cool/issues-helper or actions-cool/maintain-one-comment (by tag — anything other than a pinned full commit SHA is suspect). Capture the bun binary's hash and origin (was it downloaded from bun.sh during the run? from an attacker-controlled URL?). 2. Contain: stop the runner, revoke its registration token, rotate GITHUB_TOKEN and every workflow-accessible secret. If self-hosted, image-rebuild the runner from scratch. 3. Hunt: org-wide search for any workflow file (YAML in .github/workflows/) that uses these two actions by tag rather than by SHA; enforce a Compromised Actions Policy and pinning policy; review last 30d of commits/PRs/releases by the GITHUB_TOKEN actor on affected repos.
