GitHub workflow references actions-cool/issues-helper or maintain-one-comment by tag AIDelivery High
Hunts use of the compromised GitHub Actions in any repository referenced by tag (or by a moved-tag SHA) rather than a pinned, audited full commit SHA. Anything other than a pinned SHA on the pre-compromise commit history will pull the imposter commit on next run. Rationale: Pure-IOC supply-chain detection on the two actions named by StepSecurity and corroborated by The Hacker News (`actions-cool/issues-helper` and `actions-cool/maintain-one-comment` — same actor, identical TTP). GitHub disabled the upstream repos, but any pre-existing pinned reference by tag or by a moved-tag SHA in a workflow YAML still resolves to the imposter commit on the next run until the workflow is patched. Detection should fire at workflow-prepare time (GitHub audit logs) and again on any commit/PR that adds such a reference. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/actions-cool-issues-helper-github-action-compromised-all-tags-point-to-imposter-commit-that-exfiltrates-ci-cd-credentials • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-actions-supply-chain-attack.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/compromised-github-action-exfiltrates-workflow-credentials/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1199
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security-team test repository deliberately referencing the compromised action to validate the StepSecurity Compromised Actions Policy is working
  • Threat-research fork that retains the upstream reference for analysis purposes (should be sandboxed and offline)
  • Pinned full-commit-SHA references that map to KNOWN-GOOD pre-compromise commits (must verify the SHA pre-dates 2026-05-18 17:00 UTC and is reachable from the legitimate default branch — not the imposter dangling commit)
Response runbook
1. Triage: enumerate every repository in the org that references either action; pull the exact ref (tag, branch, or full commit SHA) used. For SHA references, verify the SHA is reachable from the repository's legitimate default-branch history (the imposter commit 1c9e803 is dangling and unreachable). 2. Contain: open emergency PRs to remove or replace the action across all affected workflows; enforce a repository ruleset that requires immutable SHA pinning on third-party actions; enable Harden-Runner or StepSecurity Compromised Actions Policy org-wide. 3. Hunt: rotate GITHUB_TOKENs and downstream secrets for any repo whose workflows ran the action since 2026-05-18 17:00 UTC; correlate against UC1 (t.m-kosche.com callbacks) to see which runners actually exfiltrated; review audit logs for unauthorized git pushes, tag manipulation, or PR creation events made by GITHUB_TOKEN actors during the affected window.

2026-05-19 13 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Active Supply Chain Attack: Malicious node-ipc Versions Published to npm StepSecurity has detected multiple malicious releases of the popular node-ipc npm package. Three versions are currently known to be compromised, containing an obfuscated payload designed to steal cloud credentials, SSH keys, and CI/CD secrets. Our team is actively analyzing the attack, and this post will be updated as our investigation progresses

Exploitation. Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Compromised node-ipc.cjs bundle write (~117KB) under node_modules · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] node-ipc C2 callback to sh.azurestaticprovider.net (May 2026 npm supply-chain) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Node.js process bulk-reading cloud & SCM credential files in single session · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
node-ipc C2 callback to sh.azurestaticprovider.net (May 2026 npm supply-chain) AICommand & Control High
Detects any DNS lookup or outbound network connection to sh.azurestaticprovider.net, the credential-exfiltration C2 used by the malicious node-ipc versions 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1 published 2026-05-14. The domain is a typosquat of azurestaticapps.net and has no legitimate business use — first sighting is incident-level signal. Rationale: Anchored on the literal C2 domain sh.azurestaticprovider.net pulled from the article's deobfuscated payload config (the 'r' field of the _0x501a65 attack config object). Domain typosquats Azure infrastructure and has no benign use — single-hit alerting tier is appropriate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-ipc
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / DFIR team intentionally resolving the domain during analysis from a sandboxed environment
  • Threat-intel feed validation tools that pre-resolve known-bad indicators (e.g. MISP, OpenCTI enrichment pipelines)
  • Internal IOC-detonation lab that mirrors npm packages to test detections
  • Network proxy doing pre-fetch / category lookup against the domain
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "VirusTotal"   // exclude analyst lookups; keep all other traffic
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify the initiating process and parent — if it's node.exe / node, immediately check `npm ls node-ipc` / `package-lock.json` on the host for versions 9.1.6, 9.2.3, or 12.0.1. Pull the node-ipc.cjs file and confirm size > 80KB. Step 2 (contain): isolate the host from network, kill the offending node process, and block sh.azurestaticprovider.net at the proxy/firewall. Treat every cloud credential present on the host (AWS, Azure, GCP, GitHub PAT, SSH key, Kube token, Terraform state, npm token) as compromised — rotate immediately. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on DeviceNetworkEvents for the same domain across the fleet for the last 30 days; pivot on DeviceFileEvents for any node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs writes since 2026-05-14; audit CI/CD job logs for npm install events of node-ipc.
// node-ipc supply-chain C2: any host contacting sh.azurestaticprovider.net
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "azurestaticprovider.net" or RemoteUrl =~ "sh.azurestaticprovider.net"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"     // exclude machine-account noise
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// node-ipc supply-chain C2 — union across DNS + CEF/firewall + ASIM tables
let SuspectDomain = "azurestaticprovider.net";
let StartTime = ago(30d);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
     | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
     | where Name has SuspectDomain
     | project TimeGenerated, Source = "DnsEvents", Host = Computer, ClientIP, QueriedName = Name, QueryType),
  (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
     | where DestinationHostName has SuspectDomain or RequestURL has SuspectDomain
     | project TimeGenerated, Source = "CommonSecurityLog", Host = SourceHostName, SrcIP = SourceIP, DstHost = DestinationHostName, DstIP = DestinationIP, URL = RequestURL),
  (ImNetworkSession
     | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
     | where DstHostname has SuspectDomain or DstDomain has SuspectDomain or Url has SuspectDomain
     | project TimeGenerated, Source = "ImNetworkSession", Host = SrcHostname, SrcIP = SrcIpAddr, DstHost = DstHostname, DstIP = DstIpAddr, URL = Url),
  (ImDnsActivity
     | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
     | where DnsQuery has SuspectDomain or DnsQueryName has SuspectDomain
     | project TimeGenerated, Source = "ImDnsActivity", Host = SrcHostname, SrcIP = SrcIpAddr, QueriedName = DnsQuery)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Malicious node-ipc Package C2 Domain Resolution (sh.azurestaticprovider.net)
id: a47c5e8e-9c21-4b1a-9b6e-b3e4c8d5f1a2
description: Detects DNS resolution or network connection to sh.azurestaticprovider.net, the credential-exfiltration C2 used by malicious node-ipc npm versions 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1 published on 2026-05-14 by the rogue maintainer atiertant. The domain typosquats Azure infrastructure and has no legitimate use.
references:

  - attack.t1041
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.exfiltration

(@QueryName:*azurestaticprovider.net* OR @DomainName:*azurestaticprovider.net* OR @DestinationHostname:*azurestaticprovider.net* OR @network.destination.name:*azurestaticprovider.net* OR @dns.question.name:*azurestaticprovider.net*)

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Compromised node-ipc.cjs bundle write (~117KB) under node_modules AIInstallation High
Detects file-write events targeting `node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs` whose payload exceeds 80KB after 2026-05-14, indicating installation of the malicious versions 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1. The clean 12.0.0 bundle was ~37KB / 1269 lines; the trojanised bundle is ~117KB / 1271 lines with an 80KB obfuscated IIFE appended after the final module.exports. Rationale: Anchored on the exact file path (`node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs`) and size delta (37KB clean → 117KB compromised, +80KB IIFE) called out in the article's diff block. The publication-date floor (2026-05-14) eliminates legitimate historical writes; the file-size predicate eliminates any future legitimate node-ipc release that doesn't add a comparable bundle. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-ipc?activeTab=versions
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Air-gapped lab environments restoring a snapshot of node-ipc 12.0.0 where prior tarball already exceeded 80KB due to legitimate fork patches
  • CI cache restoration from a vendored node_modules tarball captured pre-compromise (rare in 2026 — most teams don't vendor node_modules anymore)
  • Custom internal node-ipc fork that legitimately ships extra debug instrumentation in the .cjs bundle
  • Defender / Sysmon picking up the file write twice (rename then create) when npm rewrites the tarball — dedup on (DeviceId, FolderPath, FileSize)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("backup.exe","veeam.backup.shell.exe","snapraid.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "restore")   // exclude backup-restore noise
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): compute SHA256 of the written node-ipc.cjs and compare against the legitimate 12.0.0 hash; check the parent process — should be npm/yarn/pnpm. Confirm by `npm view node-ipc@<installed-version> dist.tarball` and inspecting the install metadata. Step 2 (contain): kill any running node process on the host, delete node_modules and package-lock.json, pin to node-ipc@11.1.0 or @12.0.0 in package.json with a npm-shrinkwrap.json lock, run `npm install --ignore-scripts` from a clean cache (`npm cache clean --force`). Treat all cloud / SCM / DB credentials accessible from this host or its CI runner as compromised — rotate. Step 3 (hunt): query DeviceFileEvents fleet-wide for the same FolderPath pattern since 2026-05-14; correlate with DNS lookups to sh.azurestaticprovider.net (UC1); audit npm audit logs / Artifactory / Verdaccio / proxy registries for the bad version tags being requested.
// Malicious node-ipc bundle write — anomalous .cjs size under node_modules
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\node-ipc\" or FolderPath has "/node_modules/node-ipc/"
| where FileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where FileSize > 80000     // clean ~37KB; trojanised ~117KB (80KB IIFE injected)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// Malicious node-ipc bundle write (ASIM file event)
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\node-ipc\" or TargetFilePath has "/node_modules/node-ipc/"
| where TargetFileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where TargetFileSize > 80000   // clean ~37KB; trojanised ~117KB
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Malicious node-ipc Bundle File Write (npm Supply Chain Compromise May 2026)
id: 8c2e4f7a-1b9d-4a3e-9c8f-2e5d7a8b9c0d
description: Detects file writes to node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs, indicating installation of the malicious node-ipc package versions 9.1.6, 9.2.3, or 12.0.1 published to npm on 2026-05-14 by the rogue maintainer account 'atiertant' (a.tiertant@atlantis-software.net). The trojanised bundle is ~117KB versus ~37KB for the legitimate 12.0.0 release.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\node_modules\node-ipc\node-ipc.cjs'
      - '/node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Custom internal fork of node-ipc with legitimately enlarged CommonJS bundle (verify SHA256 against published 12.0.0)
  - Test environments restoring known-good node-ipc tarballs from offline mirrors
level: high
(@EventID:11 source:windows.sysmon AND @TargetFilename:(*\\node_modules\\node-ipc\\node-ipc.cjs OR */node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH AND @file.path:*/node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/[\\\/]node_modules[\\\/]node-ipc[\\\/]node-ipc\.cjs$/i
| WrittenBytes>80000
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, WrittenBytes, ContextImageFileName, UserName], function={ count := count() | first := min(@timestamp) })
| first > 1747180800   // 2026-05-14T00:00:00Z epoch — only writes after publication date
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.process_name) as writer_process values(Filesystem.file_hash) as sha256 from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*node_modules*node-ipc*node-ipc.cjs" AND Filesystem.file_size>80000 AND _time>=strptime("2026-05-14","%Y-%m-%d") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_size | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.process_name) as writer_process values(Filesystem.file_hash) as sha256 from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*node_modules*node-ipc*node-ipc.cjs" AND Filesystem.file_size>80000 AND _time>=strptime("2026-05-14","%Y-%m-%d") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_size | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Node.js process bulk-reading cloud & SCM credential files in single session AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for a single node process that opens >=3 distinct categories of credential artifacts (AWS, SSH, Kubernetes, Azure, GCP, GitHub CLI, Terraform, Docker, npm, Claude / Kiro IDE, shell history) within a single process lifetime. The compromised node-ipc payload harvests over 90 categories of secrets on require() — a fan-out pattern that no legitimate node tool produces in a single session. Rationale: The article enumerates 90+ credential categories the payload sweeps — AWS, Azure, GCP, SSH, Kubernetes, GitHub CLI, Claude AI, Kiro IDE, Terraform state, shell history. Mass fan-out from a single node PID is a behaviour pattern no legitimate dev tool exhibits in a single session. Sigma omitted because the detection requires aggregation across multiple file-open events keyed by process ID. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1083 T1530
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Pulumi / AWS CDK / Terraform CDK runs — these node-based IaC tools legitimately read ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, and ~/.terraform.d/ in a single invocation
  • Backstage / Cortex / similar developer-portal CLIs that aggregate credentials for multi-cloud dashboards
  • Local dev-experience scripts (e.g. `dev login` wrappers) that source AWS + Azure + GCP creds at once for a multi-cloud session
  • VSCode + extensions launched via node.exe reading .gitconfig + .npmrc + .claude/ as part of normal IDE startup
  • Security tools themselves — Snyk / Trivy / Semgrep CLIs sometimes inspect credential files for misconfig scanning
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cdk","pulumi","terraform","snyk","trivy","semgrep","backstage","@cdktf","aws-sdk") and DistinctCredPaths < 6)   // suppress known multi-cloud IaC tooling unless fan-out is very wide
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify the node process — pull its full command line and working directory; check whether node-ipc is in the resolved module graph (`lsof -p <pid> | grep node-ipc` on Linux, ProcessExplorer on Windows). Cross-check the host against UC1 (sh.azurestaticprovider.net contact) and UC2 (compromised .cjs file on disk). Step 2 (contain): if any of UC1/UC2 corroborate, kill the node process, isolate the host, and rotate every credential whose file was opened (start with cloud root/IAM keys, GitHub PATs, SSH keys, kube admin tokens). Step 3 (hunt): list every host the same user identity has touched in the last 30 days (lateral exposure); search for outbound HTTPS to any new azure-themed subdomain since 2026-05-14; audit private repos and cloud resources for the rotated credentials' last-used activity to identify what the attacker already accessed.
// node process touching multiple credential-store paths in one session — post-require('node-ipc') harvest pattern
let CredPathSubstrings = dynamic([
    @"\.aws\credentials", @"\.aws\config",
    @"\.ssh\id_rsa", @"\.ssh\id_ed25519", @"\.ssh\id_ecdsa", @"\.ssh\known_hosts",
    @"\.kube\config",
    @"\.azure\accessTokens", @"\.azure\azureProfile",
    @"\.config\gcloud\", @"\.config\gh\",
    @"\.terraform.d\", @"\.docker\config.json",
    @"\.npmrc", @"\.netrc", @"\.gitconfig",
    @"\.claude\", @"\.kiro\",
    @"\.bash_history", @"\.zsh_history", @"\.psql_history",
    "/.aws/", "/.ssh/", "/.kube/", "/.azure/",
    "/.config/gcloud/", "/.config/gh/", "/.terraform.d/",
    "/.docker/config.json", "/.npmrc", "/.netrc", "/.gitconfig",
    "/.claude/", "/.kiro/", "/.bash_history", "/.zsh_history"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, FileName)
| where FullPath has_any (CredPathSubstrings)
| summarize DistinctCredPaths = dcount(FullPath),
            CredFilesSample = make_set(FullPath, 30),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmdLine = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCreationTime, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where DistinctCredPaths >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
// node process touching multiple credential-store paths in one session (ASIM file event)
let CredPathSubstrings = dynamic([
    @"\.aws\credentials", @"\.aws\config",
    @"\.ssh\id_rsa", @"\.ssh\id_ed25519", @"\.ssh\id_ecdsa",
    @"\.kube\config", @"\.azure\accessTokens", @"\.azure\azureProfile",
    @"\.config\gcloud\", @"\.config\gh\", @"\.terraform.d\",
    @"\.docker\config.json", @"\.npmrc", @"\.netrc", @"\.gitconfig",
    @"\.claude\", @"\.kiro\", @"\.bash_history", @"\.zsh_history",
    "/.aws/", "/.ssh/", "/.kube/", "/.azure/",
    "/.config/gcloud/", "/.config/gh/", "/.terraform.d/",
    "/.docker/config.json", "/.npmrc", "/.netrc", "/.gitconfig",
    "/.claude/", "/.kiro/", "/.bash_history", "/.zsh_history"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","/node","\\node")
| extend FullPath = TargetFilePath
| where FullPath has_any (CredPathSubstrings)
| summarize DistinctCredPaths = dcount(FullPath),
            CredFilesSample = make_set(FullPath, 30),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleCmdLine = any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
            by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActorUsername
| where DistinctCredPaths >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
(@process.name:(node OR node.exe) OR @process.executable.name:(node OR node.exe)) AND (@file.path:(*/.aws/credentials* OR */.aws/config* OR */.ssh/id_rsa* OR */.ssh/id_ed25519* OR */.ssh/id_ecdsa* OR */.kube/config* OR */.azure/accessTokens* OR */.azure/azureProfile* OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.config/gh/* OR */.terraform.d/* OR */.docker/config.json OR */.npmrc OR */.netrc OR */.gitconfig OR */.claude/* OR */.kiro/* OR */.bash_history OR */.zsh_history) OR @auditd.SYSCALL.path:(*/.aws/credentials* OR */.ssh/id_rsa* OR */.kube/config* OR */.azure/* OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.terraform.d/* OR */.docker/config.json OR */.npmrc OR */.netrc OR */.gitconfig OR */.claude/* OR */.kiro/*))
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/[\\\/]node(\.exe)?$/i
| TargetFileName=/(\.aws[\\\/](credentials|config)|\.ssh[\\\/]id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|\.kube[\\\/]config|\.azure[\\\/](accessTokens|azureProfile)|\.config[\\\/](gcloud|gh)[\\\/]|\.terraform\.d[\\\/]|\.docker[\\\/]config\.json|\.npmrc|\.netrc|\.gitconfig|\.claude[\\\/]|\.kiro[\\\/]|\.bash_history|\.zsh_history)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, UserName], function={ DistinctCredFiles := count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true) | sampleFiles := collect([TargetFileName], limit=30) | first := min(@timestamp) | last := max(@timestamp) })
| DistinctCredFiles >= 3
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_cred_files values(Filesystem.file_path) as files_sample min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_ed25519*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_ecdsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/accessTokens*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/azureProfile*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.terraform.d/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.netrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.gitconfig*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.claude/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kiro/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bash_history*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.zsh_history*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_guid Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_cred_files >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_cred_files values(Filesystem.file_path) as files_sample min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_ed25519*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_ecdsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/accessTokens*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/azureProfile*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.terraform.d/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.netrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.gitconfig*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.claude/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kiro/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.bash_history*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.zsh_history*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_guid Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_cred_files >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("sh.azurestaticprovider.net")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["sh.azurestaticprovider.net"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("sh.azurestaticprovider.net")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("sh.azurestaticprovider.net")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("sh.azurestaticprovider.net")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("sh.azurestaticprovider.net")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bf9d8c0c3ed3ceaa831a13de27f1b1c7c7b7f01d2db4103bfdba4191940b0301") or SHA1 in~ ("bf9d8c0c3ed3ceaa831a13de27f1b1c7c7b7f01d2db4103bfdba4191940b0301") or MD5 in~ ("bf9d8c0c3ed3ceaa831a13de27f1b1c7c7b7f01d2db4103bfdba4191940b0301")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bf9d8c0c3ed3ceaa831a13de27f1b1c7c7b7f01d2db4103bfdba4191940b0301") or SHA1 in~ ("bf9d8c0c3ed3ceaa831a13de27f1b1c7c7b7f01d2db4103bfdba4191940b0301") or MD5 in~ ("bf9d8c0c3ed3ceaa831a13de27f1b1c7c7b7f01d2db4103bfdba4191940b0301")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["bf9d8c0c3ed3ceaa831a13de27f1b1c7c7b7f01d2db4103bfdba4191940b0301"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud npm preinstall hook spawning bun runtime AIInstallation High
Detects npm/node spawning the bun JavaScript runtime to execute a root-level index.js — the exact lifecycle pattern the May 2026 AntV supply-chain attack uses to fire 498KB obfuscated payload during npm install of @antv/g6, echarts-for-react, size-sensor, timeago.js and 319 other packages. bun is rarely a legitimate npm child in enterprise CI/dev environments. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim 'preinstall': 'bun run index.js' lifecycle hook combined with the article's named parent context (npm install). Bun-as-child-of-npm has near-zero legitimate baseline in dev/CI fleets outside the Bun ecosystem itself. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Bun-native projects where bun is genuinely listed as a runtime dependency (rare; usually invoked as bunx not via index.js)
  • Developer testing a local index.js script via bun in a node_modules-bootstrap shell where npm-init ran moments earlier
  • Internal supply-chain self-hosting where a vetted private package legitimately uses bun as a build tool
  • CI image building tests using bun runner to validate node packages
  • Monorepo tooling like Turborepo orchestrating mixed runtimes
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ignore-scripts","bunx ") and ProcessCommandLine !has "preinstall") | where not (FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Bun\\" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "explorer.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — pull the SHA256 of the bun binary and the parent npm command. Identify the package and version being installed (look at InitiatingProcessParentCommandLine or recent npm-cli.log on host). Cross-reference the package against the 323 AntV-wave compromised package list. Step 2: Contain — isolate host via Defender Live Response or CrowdStrike RTR. Kill the bun process tree. Block outbound to t.m-kosche.com at egress proxy. If on a developer workstation with cloud credentials present, immediately rotate all AWS/GCP/Azure/GitHub/npm tokens that were on disk. Step 3: Hunt — query DeviceFileEvents for .claude/, .vscode/, ~/.local/share/kitty/ writes by the same InitiatingProcessId. Pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for api.github.com and t.m-kosche.com beacons from this host. Check for new repos under the user's GitHub account with Dune-themed names.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm","npm.exe","node","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","yarn install","pnpm install")
| where FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "index.js"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","/npm","/node")
    or CommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","yarn install","pnpm install")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\bun.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/bun"
| where CommandLine has "index.js"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, AccountName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects npm/node spawning the bun JavaScript runtime to execute index.js, the preinstall lifecycle loader used by the Mini Shai-Hulud AntV supply-chain compromise (May 2026).
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.007

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\bun.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'index.js'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe) @Image:(*\\bun.exe OR *\\Bun.exe OR *\\BUN.EXE) @CommandLine:*index.js*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(npm|node|npx|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/\\bun\.exe$/i CommandLine=/index\.js/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Mini Shai-Hulud Claude Code SessionStart hook injection via npm install AIInstallation High
Detects npm/node/bun writing .claude/settings.json or .claude/setup.mjs, the AI-coding-agent hijack used by the AntV wave to re-execute the credential-harvesting payload every time a developer opens a new Claude Code session in an infected workspace. Legitimate Claude Code settings are authored by the user via the IDE, never by an install lifecycle process. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim persistence path '.claude/settings.json with a SessionStart hook executing node .claude/setup.mjs'. Pairing the file path with an npm-family writer is high-fidelity because Claude Code settings are normally authored by Code.exe / claude CLI itself, never by node during an install. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1546 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate npm-installed dev tool that genuinely modifies .claude config (e.g. claude-mem MCP plugin auto-config — rare and should be allowlisted explicitly)
  • Postinstall script of an enterprise-vetted CLI that writes .claude/settings.json for organization defaults
  • Developer running 'claude /init' which spawns node to template settings.json (different parent chain — explorer.exe, not npm)
  • Dotfile-management tools (chezmoi, dotbot) syncing .claude config — parent is chezmoi/python, not npm
  • Internal scaffolding generator that writes .claude/settings.json once per repo clone
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chezmoi.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "dotbot") | where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "claude /init" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "Code.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — read the contents of the written .claude/settings.json. Look for 'SessionStart' hook keys and 'node .claude/setup.mjs' commands. Hash .claude/setup.mjs and check for the 498KB obfuscated-bun signature. Step 2: Contain — isolate host. Delete .claude/settings.json and .claude/setup.mjs. Run 'npm install --ignore-scripts' guidance to user. If a Claude Code session ran after the file was written, treat the developer as token-compromised — rotate npm publish tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS/GCP/Azure CLI tokens immediately. Step 3: Hunt — pivot to .vscode/tasks.json writes by same InitiatingProcessId; check ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py and ~/.config/systemd/user/*.service for sibling persistence. Search GitHub Audit for new repos under user's account with Dune-themed names. Confirm no api.github.com/search/commits polling from python on host.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.claude\" or FolderPath has "/.claude/")
| where FileName in~ ("settings.json","setup.mjs","settings.local.json")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","bun.exe","npm","node","bun")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\.claude\\settings.json","/.claude/settings.json","\\.claude\\setup.mjs","/.claude/setup.mjs","\\.claude\\settings.local.json")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","node","bun","yarn","pnpm","npx")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

VS Code tasks.json folderOpen persistence written by npm install chain AIInstallation Medium
Detects npm/node/bun writing .vscode/tasks.json, the IDE-folderOpen persistence used by the Mini Shai-Hulud AntV wave so the payload re-executes whenever a developer opens the project workspace in VS Code. Legitimate tasks.json is authored by the IDE itself or committed by humans, not by npm install. Rationale: Anchored on article's '.vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen' persistence claim. Legitimate tasks.json writes come from Code.exe / human edit; npm-as-writer is the discriminator. Hunting tier because some legitimate npm scaffolders (e.g. create-react-app variants) do write workspace tasks — but in combination with the .claude UC firing on same InitiatingProcessId, confidence escalates. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • create-react-app / create-next-app / Vite scaffolders writing tasks.json on project init
  • npm-installed dev tool extension that legitimately templates workspace tasks (e.g. nx CLI workspace generators)
  • Yeoman generator (yo) running under node and producing tasks.json
  • Internal monorepo bootstrap script invoked by npm postinstall
  • VSCode dev container CLI writing workspace configs via node
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("create-react-app","create-next-app","vite create","nx generate","yo ")) | where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "Code.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — read the tasks.json content. Hunt for 'runOn': 'folderOpen' combined with shell-command tasks pointing to node /.claude/setup.mjs, bun run index.js, or python ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py. Confirm the package that triggered the write by walking InitiatingProcessParentId chain to the npm install invocation. Step 2: Contain — delete the malicious tasks.json or revert to the committed version (git checkout). If the developer has opened the workspace in VS Code since the write, treat the host as actively executing the payload and isolate. Step 3: Hunt — correlate to the .claude/settings.json UC and kitty/cat.py UC on same DeviceId. Audit recent npm install history (~/.npm/_logs/) for the compromised AntV package versions.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.vscode\" or FolderPath has "/.vscode/")
| where FileName =~ "tasks.json"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","bun.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\.vscode\\tasks.json","/.vscode/tasks.json")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","node","bun","yarn","pnpm","npx")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mini Shai-Hulud Linux daemon persistence: kitty/cat.py and systemd user service AIInstallation High
Detects creation of ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py or ~/.config/systemd/user/*.service by an npm/node/bun process — the OS-level Linux persistence chain that polls GitHub commit search hourly for 'firedalazer'-keyword commands signed with the attacker's 4096-bit RSA-PSS public key. The cat.py + systemd unit combination is article-specific and has near-zero legitimate baseline. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim '~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py' and 'systemd user service' persistence path. The path is misleading by design (looks like the kitty terminal cache) but kitty itself never writes cat.py. Combined with an npm-family writer, the FP rate is effectively zero. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • kitty terminal config writes (kitty.conf, sessions/, themes/) — different filenames, kitty.py would never write a cat.py
  • systemd user service installs by user-level package managers (pipx, cargo install --user, snap) — different writer process
  • Developer manually installing a personal cron-replacement systemd unit (writer is text editor or systemctl, not node)
  • Linux dotfile-management bootstrap (chezmoi apply) writing systemd user units
  • Internal Linux configuration management agent (Ansible-pull as user) — parent is ansible-playbook
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pipx install","cargo install","snap install","systemctl --user enable")) | where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemctl","systemd-run"))
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — read cat.py and the .service unit. Look for ExecStart pointing at 'python3 ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py' and the script body should reference api.github.com/search/commits and 'firedalazer' keyword. Capture SHA256 of cat.py. Step 2: Contain — 'systemctl --user stop' and 'disable' the service unit. Delete cat.py and the .service file. Kill any running python process whose cmdline references cat.py. Treat all credentials accessible to this user account (cloud CLIs, kubeconfig, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/id_*) as compromised — rotate immediately. Step 3: Hunt — search for outbound to t.m-kosche.com from this host (primary C2), api.github.com /search/commits polling, and process events showing python3 reading ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.gcp/credentials, ~/.kube/config. Pivot to GitHub Audit for repo.create events under the user's account.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath has "/.local/share/kitty/" and FileName =~ "cat.py")
    or (FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user/" and FileName endswith ".service")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm","node","bun","yarn","pnpm","npx","sh","bash","dash","zsh")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm","node","bun")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentWriter = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (TargetFilePath has "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user/" and TargetFilePath endswith ".service")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","node","bun","yarn","pnpm","sh","bash","dash","zsh")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud Linux daemon persistence — kitty/cat.py + systemd user service
id: 9c3f4e2d-7a1b-4e8c-9f3a-6d5e2b8a4c1f
description: Detects creation of ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py or a ~/.config/systemd/user/*.service unit by npm/node/bun — the Linux OS-level persistence chain used by the Mini Shai-Hulud AntV wave to poll the GitHub commit search API for firedalazer-keyword commands.
references:

  selection_systemd:

    TargetFilename|endswith: '.service'
